senses.gloss: भिक्षणम् [bhikṣaṇam], [भिक्ष्-ल्युट्] Begging, begging alms, mendicancy.
भिक्षा [bhikṣā], [भिक्ष्-अ]
Asking, begging, soliciting वृत्ते शराव- संपाते भिक्षां नित्यं यतिश्चरेत् Ms.6.56.
Anything given as alms, alms; भवति भिक्षां देहि.
Wages, hire.
Service.

A means of subsistence अपेतक्लमसंतापाः सुभिक्षाः सुप्रतिश्रयाः Rām.2.92.6. -Comp. -अटनम् wandering about begging for alms; रुद्रो येन कपालपाणिपुटके भिक्षाटनं कारितः Bh.2.95. (-नः) a beggar, mendicant. -अन्नम् food obtained by begging, alms. -अयनम् (णम्) = भिक्षाटन q. v. -अर्थिन् a. begging for alms or charity. (-m.) a beggar. -अर्ह a. worthy of alms, a fit object of charity. -अशनम् the food obtained by begging; भिक्षाशनं तदपि नीरसमेकवारम् Bh.3.19. -आशिन् a.
living on alms; भिक्षाशी जनमध्य- संगरहितः Bh.3.86.

dishonest. -आहारः begged food; Bh.3.144. -उपजीविन् a. living on alms, a beggar.-करणम् asking alms, begging. -चरः, -चारः a beggar or mendicant. -चरणम्, -चर्यम्, -चर्या wandering about begging for alms. -पात्रम् a begging-bowl, an alms-dish; so भिक्षाभाण्डम्, भिक्षाभाजनम्. -भुज् a. living on alms. -माणवः a young beggar (used as a term of contempt); P.VI.2.69 com. -वासस् n. a beggar's dress. -वृत्तिः f. living by begging, a mendicant's life.
भिक्षाकः [bhikṣākḥ], (-की f.) A beggar, mendicant; P.III.2.155.
भिक्षित [bhikṣita], p. p. Begged, asked, &c.
भिक्षुः [bhikṣuḥ], [भिक्ष्-उन्]
A beggar, mendicant in general; भिक्षां च भिक्षवे दद्यात् Ms.3.94.
A religious mendicant, a Brāhmaṇa in the fourth order of his religious life (when he quits his house and family and lives only on alms), a Sannyāsin.
The fourth order stage in the religious life of a Brāhmaṇa (संन्यास).

A Buddhist mendicant. -Comp. -चर्या begging, a mendicant's life.-भावः monk-hood, priest-hood. -सङ्घः a society of Buddhist mendicants. -सङ्घाती old or tattered clothes (चीवर). -सूत्रम् a collection of rules for mendicants; P.IV.3.11.
भिक्षुकः [bhikṣukḥ], [भिक्ष्-उक] A beggar, mendicant; आकीर्णं भिक्षुकैर्वान्यैरगारमुपसंव्रजेत् Ms.6.51. -की A female mendicant; cf. भिक्षुणी A Buddhist nun.
भिक्ष् [bhikṣ], 1 Ā. (भिक्षते, भिक्षित)
To ask, beg or ask for (with two acc.); भिक्षमाणो वनं प्रियाम् Bk.6.9.
To beg. (as alms); न यज्ञार्थं धनं शूद्राद्विप्रो भिक्षेत कर्हिचित् Ms. 11.24,25.
To ask without obtaining.
To be weary or distressed.
To obtain.
